newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam gives low-key welcome to Albright.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam gives low-key welcome to Albright.

text.p: Vietnam gave a low-key welcome to U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday, dispensing with the flag waiving and media coverage which normally covers senior level diplomatic visits.
State-controlled media was largely empty of either news or comment about only the second visit by an American Secretary of State to Vietnam since the Vietnam war ended in 1975.
The streets of the capital were similarly bare of flags.
Albright arrived in Vietnam late on Thursday for a visit which was extended at short notice following a U.S. decision to cancel a subsequent trip to Cambodia because of security concerns.

Instead of leaving for Phnom Penh late on Friday, as originally scheduled, she will stay overnight in Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, before heading to Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's June 30 handover to China.

Albright began her formal duties here by visiting the United States' two-year-old embassy in Hanoi and the U.S. liaison office which serves as the headquarters here for Washington's efforts to account for the 2,100 U.S. servicemen listed as missing-in-action.
She was due to attend a formal welcoming ceremony later, witness signing of a copyright accord and meet Prime minister Vo Van Kiet for talks expected to cover economic relations and human rights.
Albright's predecessor, Warren Christopher, made a breakthrough visit to Vietnam in 1995 to officiate at events surrounding the normalisation of diplomatic ties between the former enemies.
Since then progress in relations has been slow and the two countries have yet to achieve full trade and economic normalisation.
